chapter: Zach White, Cotton Pickers and Cab Calloway
title: Joining Zach White's band in Columbus, with Sy Oliver writing
summary: In spring 1933 he joined Zach White in Columbus, Ohio, where Sy Oliver was the band's writer; Barefield credits Oliver with taking the style to Lunceford and Tommy Dorsey.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Okay, so let's get back to Zach White in Columbus.
So now I joined Zach White.

1933 in the spring. And we were stationed in Columbus, Ohio. And Sy Oliver was there and Dick Dickenson and Slim Rhodes and Eli Robinson and -- these are trombone players. I only see -- the saxophone player, it was me -- I never could remember this whole saxophone section we had. I know Ben Smith -- Ben Richardson was there. But the tenor player I can't remember unless it was -- I don't think it was Delbert Lee, but we had a tenor player. And we only had three saxes at that time.

Sy was writing. In fact, Sy was the band. And Sy was the Jimmy Lunceford band. I mean, Sy took all of this stuff from one place to the other and it was Sy Oliver. I mean, you have to give him credit for that. He had developed a style and it became a great style of writing. And he took it from Zach White and took it to Jimmy Lunceford. And then he left Jimmy Lunceford and took it to Tommy Dorsey's band.
